# Results — Study 129 (Heikin-Ashi) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — Heikin-Ashi
colour-flip signal on daily bars, enter at the next bar's open **in the direction of the
flip**, exit on a symmetric take-profit/stop of **±1 ATR(20)**, max hold 60 bars — run
across a basket of four liquid instruments (SPY, QQQ, IWM, AAPL) and pinned against
a **random-direction control** on the *same* entries AND the **raw-candle colour-flip**
equivalent (the unsmoothed baseline). 15 years of Yahoo daily bars. As-of
**2026-06-14**; match the per-tape fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.
Trades pooled across the basket: **n = 3,924** (~65.4/instrument/year).*

## The honest test — symmetric ±1 ATR, gross (cost = 0)

A direction-symmetric payoff is the only fair way to ask *"does the HA flip point the
right way?"* — with TP and SL equidistant, a coin earns ≈ 0.

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **HA colour flip (with the flip)** | 3,924 | **50.7%** | **+1.37** | — | **+0.56** |
| Random direction (control) | 3,924 | 49.4% | +1.02 | — | +0.33 |
| Raw-candle colour flip (baseline) | 7,602 | 49.3% | −2.45 | — | −1.55 |

- The HA flip's gross expectancy is **+1.37 bps/trade** at HAC *t* = **+0.56** —
  statistically **indistinguishable from zero**.
- It does **not beat the coin**. HA − random = **+0.35 bps/trade**; well inside noise.
  The bootstrap 95% CI on the annualised Sharpe is **[−0.15, +0.26]** (30.8% of
  resamples negative — the Sharpe is not significantly different from zero).
- **The smoothing actually costs signal.** HA has ~984 flips per ticker vs ~1,910 raw
  flips: it filters noise but *also* filters the mean-reversion signal in the raw
  candles (raw *t* = −1.55 is at least a directional signal, though also sub-threshold
  and in the *wrong* direction for the folk claim).

## The long-only illusion — bull-market drift masquerading as signal

The per-instrument split reveals a structural confound:

| Arm | Long trades | mean (bps) | *t* | Short trades | mean (bps) | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **HA flip** | 1,962 | +17.57 | +3.67 | 1,962 | −14.83 | −3.19 |
| **Random control** | 1,967 | +16.87 | +3.35 | 1,957 | −14.91 | −2.95 |

Both longs and the random longs show t > 3 — this is the **bull-market drift of 15
years of equity markets, not HA signal**. The random control's longs perform *nearly
identically* to the HA longs (+16.87 vs +17.57 bps, Δ = +0.70 bps), confirming the
long-side apparent edge is entirely market-direction exposure, not HA skill.

## Per-instrument breakdown

| Ticker | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* | HA flips | raw flips |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 976 | 53.0% | +8.04 | +2.24 | 984 | 1,898 |
| QQQ  | 972 | 50.0% | −0.48 | −0.10 | 979 | 1,910 |
| IWM  | 1,033 | 50.0% | −0.05 | −0.01 | 1,040 | 1,916 |
| AAPL | 943 | 50.1% | −2.08 | −0.34 | 947 | 1,921 |

SPY's *t* = +2.24 looks interesting in isolation — but the SPY random control yields a
mean of +2.19 bps (*t* = +0.52), with seed-to-seed range [−8.32, +5.27] over 20 seeds.
The HA flip's +8.04 does exceed the mean random — but this is a single-instrument,
single-outcome result (not pre-specified, post-hoc), and QQQ/IWM/AAPL show no such
pattern. Pooling 3,924 trades kills the signal (t = +0.56).

## Could you trade it? — the cost sweep

At ~65 trades/instrument/year (moderate turnover), costs erode what little positive
gross there is rapidly:

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* | approximate effect |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +1.37 | +0.56 | not different from zero |
| 0.5 bps | +0.87 | +0.36 | noise |
| 1.0 bps | +0.37 | +0.15 | noise |
| 2.0 bps | −0.63 | −0.26 | noise |
| 5.0 bps | −3.63 | −1.49 | significant loser |

Even the gross edge (+1.37 bps) is not statistically significant, so there is no
break-even cost that justifies the strategy — the gross is not significantly above zero
to begin with.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic daily tape (`data.synthetic_daily`), the same engine recovers
a HA colour-flip edge **only when bar-level momentum is planted**, and reads ≈ 0 when
it isn't — confirming the rule is a faithful momentum harvester, and that the real daily
tape simply has no persistent directional structure for it to harvest:

| Planted bar AR(1) momentum | HA gross (bps/trade) | beats random control? |
|---|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (martingale) | ≈ 0 (coin) | no |
| +0.10 (persistence) | positive | yes |
| −0.10 (reversion) | negative | no (wrong side) |

HA also produces systematically fewer flips than raw candles (about half as many), which
confirms the "smoothing" claim — but smoothing adds lag, not forecasting skill.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Pooled gross HAC *t* = +0.56 on 3,924 trades; Δ vs random control
  +0.35 bps (noise); bootstrap Sharpe CI [−0.15, +0.26]. The apparent long-side signal
  (*t* = +3.67) is replicated almost identically by a random control (*t* = +3.35),
  confirming it is bull-market drift, not HA skill. No evidence that the smoothed-candle
  colour flip carries any directional information beyond market-direction exposure.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The gross is not significantly positive; at 1 bp round-trip
  cost the signal completely disappears (*t* = +0.15). No positive break-even cost exists.
- **Smoothing adds lag, not signal.** HA flips at roughly half the rate of raw candles,
  which the folk claim presents as a virtue ("filters noise"). But the signal comparison
  confirms the delay that comes with smoothing gives no directional advantage over a coin.
